title: Forms deep dive — ControlValueAccessor, async validators, complex patterns
exp: Beyond the basics, interviewers test ControlValueAccessor (create a custom form control), async validators (server-side email check), and cross-field validation. These are the patterns that appear in UI library and enterprise form-heavy Angular work.
pts: `FormGroup`, `FormControl`, `FormArray` — the three building blocks of Reactive Forms
**Typed Forms** (Angular 14+): `FormGroup<{email: FormControl<string>}>` — TypeScript knows the shape of each control; use `nonNullable: true` to avoid `T | null` types
**Custom validator:** `ValidatorFn` that returns `ValidationErrors | null` — return `null` for valid, an object for invalid
**Cross-field validator:** set on a `FormGroup`, receives the entire group — use to compare two fields (passwords match, date range valid)
**Async validator:** `AsyncValidatorFn` returning `Observable<ValidationErrors | null>` — debounce to avoid hammering the server on every keystroke
**`updateOn`:** control when validation runs: `updateOn: 'change'` (default), `'blur'` (after leaving field), `'submit'` (on form submit only)
**`ControlValueAccessor`:** interface that makes a custom component work as a native form control — implement `writeValue`, `registerOnChange`, `registerOnTouched`, provide `NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR`
**`getRawValue()` vs `value`:** `value` excludes disabled controls; `getRawValue()` includes them — use getRawValue() when submitting to avoid losing disabled field data
pr: Build a star rating ControlValueAccessor that works with Reactive Forms

qa.q: What is ControlValueAccessor and when do you need to implement it?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** ControlValueAccessor is an interface that bridges a custom component to Angular's form API, making it usable as a form control with both Reactive Forms and template-driven Forms. You implement it when you're building a custom input component (star rating, color picker, address form, rich text editor) that should participate in form validation and value binding. Implement writeValue (receive value from form), registerOnChange (notify form of changes), registerOnTouched (notify form of blur), and provide NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR via multi-provider.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: What is the difference between form.value and form.getRawValue()?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** form.value excludes disabled controls — their values are omitted from the object. form.getRawValue() includes all controls including disabled ones. This matters when you disable a field for UI reasons (e.g., "confirmation email is read-only") but still need its value when submitting. If you use form.value to build the submit payload, you'll silently lose the disabled field's value. Always use getRawValue() when building the submit payload.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Transient creates a new instance on every request; Scoped creates one instance per HTTP request container; Singleton lives for the app domain lifespan. Capturing a Scoped service inside a Singleton captures the DbContext across requests, causing concurrency bugs.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Instantiating new HttpClient() instances manually causes socket exhaustion in OS TIME_WAIT state under high concurrency. Fix: register typed clients with IHttpClientFactory to manage handler lifetimes and DNS refresh.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** IHttpClientFactory prevents socket leaks and manages DNS rotation, but requires explicit Polly retry and circuit breaker policies to prevent cascade failures during downstream outages.

qa.q: How do you implement an async validator that checks if an email is already taken?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** Create an AsyncValidatorFn that returns an Observable<ValidationErrors | null>: take the control value, debounce to avoid hitting the API on every keystroke, call the API, map the response to null (valid) or { emailTaken: true } (invalid). Always add catchError(() => of(null)) so an API failure doesn't break the form. The form control shows status PENDING while the async validator is running. Attach it with asyncValidators in the FormControl constructor.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Async methods compile into an IAsyncStateMachine struct managed by the AsyncMethodBuilder. Awaiting an uncompleted task yields execution back to the caller. Blocking with .Result on a thread bound to a SynchronizationContext causes deadlocks when the continuation waits for the blocked thread.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Sync-over-async (.Result or .Wait()) on ASP.NET request threads rapidly exhausts thread pool threads, leading to HTTP 503 gateway timeouts and request queuing under load.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Async all the way preserves thread pool scalability, but requires passing CancellationToken through all layers and avoiding sync blocking methods everywhere.

qa.q: What is a cross-field validator and how do you apply it?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** A cross-field validator is a ValidatorFn applied to a FormGroup (not a single FormControl) that can compare multiple fields. Example: passwords match validator receives the entire FormGroup, reads group.get('password')?.value and group.get('confirmPassword')?.value, returns null if they match or { passwordMismatch: true } if not. Apply it in the FormGroup constructor's second argument: new FormGroup({...}, { validators: [passwordMatchValidator] }). Check the error on the group: form.errors?.'passwordMismatch'.

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** Operating What is a cross-field validator and how do you apply it? at scale requires understanding the runtime lifecycle, memory allocations, and underlying execution constraints. The underlying framework or storage engine optimizes execution when contracts are explicitly preserved.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Un-handled edge cases in What is a cross-field validator and how do you apply it? under high concurrent traffic can lead to performance degradation, unhandled exceptions, or unexpected memory growth. Always enforce defensive validation and error handling.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** Choosing this implementation approach balances developer velocity and system performance. Senior engineers evaluate latency, operational overhead, and maintenance costs before committing.

qa.q: What is updateOn and what are the three options?
qa.a:
**Elevator Pitch:** updateOn controls when Angular runs validation and updates the form control value. 'change' (default): validates on every keystroke — good for instant feedback. 'blur': validates when the user leaves the field — reduces unnecessary validation noise during typing. 'submit': validates only when the form is submitted — best for sensitive fields where showing errors while typing feels intrusive. Set it per-control: new FormControl('', { updateOn: 'blur' }) or per-group: new FormGroup({...}, { updateOn: 'blur' }).

**Under the Hood & Mechanics:** EF Core builds an Expression Tree, translates it via the relational SQL provider into a parameterized T-SQL query, and materializes entities into the DbContext Change Tracker. N+1 queries occur when navigating un-included navigation properties in a loop.

**Production Failure Mode & Gotcha:** Executing queries without AsNoTracking() in read-only APIs forces EF Core to keep snapshot copies of all returned entities in memory, causing high RAM usage and CPU tracking overhead.

**Senior Trade-Off Signal:** AsNoTracking() speeds up read queries by 20-30% and reduces memory footprint, but disables identity resolution and automatic change tracking for updates.
